name: com.jaybirddigital/website
title: Jaybird Digital
description: Build and publish a website from a chat. No account or API key needed; you get a live link to share.

tools.name: start_website
tools.description: Creates a new, empty website and returns its websiteId, the editKey for changing it, the viewUrl where it can be seen, the keepUrl where the person keeps it, photoLink (a link where the person adds their own photos), siteZip (an address an AI that can run commands sends the whole website to as one zip, photos included), and the rules and size limits its files must meet. Each call makes a separate website; to change one already started, save to its websiteId instead. No account is needed: a draft lasts 7 days unless the person keeps it, and with an account connected it joins that account.

businessName.description: The website's name as the person gave it, such as their business's name. It is shown in the website's address.

about.description: Optional: what the person said the website is for, in their words.

tools.name: save_website_files
tools.description: Adds or replaces files on a website and checks every page against the rules start_website returned. Files not sent stay as they are; delete_website_file removes one, and edit_website_file changes part of one. Never send a photo here as base64: one photo is hundreds of thousands of characters, slow and costly to write; the person adds photos at the photoLink start_website returned, and save_website_pictures saves pictures you hold as files or at an https address. If you can run commands with internet access, write the website in a folder and send it all at once, photos included, to siteZip instead of typing every file here. Returns the viewUrl, keepUrl, pages, passed, and problems naming each rule a page breaks; the person can keep the website once passed is true. A website holds up to 40 files and 12 MB, with pages up to 300 KB and other files up to 2 MB.

websiteId.description: The websiteId start_website returned, or one list_sites shows.

editKey.description: The editKey start_website returned, which proves the website is the caller's. Leave it out for a website in the connected account.

files.description: 1 to 40 files to add or replace. A file whose path is already saved is overwritten.

path.description: The file's path from the website's root: lower-case, up to four folders deep, such as index.html, about.html, styles.css or images/shop.jpg. index.html is the home page, and the address /about serves about.html.

content.description: The file's text, or base64 for a small picture you made (an icon) or a font. Not for photos: see photoLink and save_website_pictures.

encoding.description: base64 for pictures and fonts. Text is utf8.

tools.name: edit_website_file
tools.description: Changes part of one saved page, stylesheet or script in place: each edit replaces its find text with its replace text, so a fix sends only the text it changes instead of the whole file. Copy find exactly from the file (read_website_file shows it); it must appear once, or set all to change every one. Edits apply in order, and if any fails nothing is saved. Every page is then checked against the rules, and it returns the same report as save_website_files with edited. Fails with not_in_file when a find text is not there, found_more_than_once when it is there several times, and not_text for a picture or font. To add a file or replace a whole one, use save_website_files.

websiteId.description: The websiteId start_website returned, or one list_sites shows.

editKey.description: The editKey start_website returned, which proves the website is the caller's. Leave it out for a website in the connected account.

path.description: The file's path from the website's root, exactly as it was saved, such as index.html, about.html or images/shop.jpg. list_website_files shows every path.

edits.description: 1 to 20 changes to the file, applied in order.

find.description: The exact text to change, copied from the file, with enough around it to appear only once.

replace.description: What the text becomes. Empty removes it.

all.description: true to change every place find appears. Leave it out to change one, which must be the only one.

tools.name: save_website_pictures
tools.description: Saves pictures the person gave you, such as photos they uploaded in the conversation, as files on a website, without sending their bytes as text: pass each one as a file in pictures and it is downloaded from its download_url. ChatGPT fills the file in itself; any AI can also pass a picture's public https address as download_url, with file_id any name for it. Each is saved as images/ unless paths names another place, and a large picture is made smaller to suit a web page. Returns saved, each picture's path and size to use as an src in the pages, beside the same report as save_website_files. Up to 10 pictures a call. Fails with picture_unreachable when a download address has expired (pass the file again) and not_a_picture for anything but a JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF. For a website with a plan, use upload_image instead.

websiteId.description: The websiteId start_website returned, or one list_sites shows.

editKey.description: The editKey start_website returned, which proves the website is the caller's. Leave it out for a website in the connected account.

download_url.description: Where the picture can be downloaded: filled in by ChatGPT for a file the person uploaded, or any https address of a picture the person may use.

file_id.description: The file's id as ChatGPT gives it; for a picture at an address, any short label.

mime_type.description: The file's type, such as image/jpeg, when it is known.

file_name.description: The file's name as the person uploaded it, such as storefront.jpg, when it is known.

pictures.description: 1 to 10 pictures, each a file: ChatGPT fills in download_url and file_id for a file the person uploaded; another AI passes a picture's public https address as download_url.

paths.description: Optional: where to save each picture, in the same order as pictures, such as images/gallery-1.jpg. The extension follows the picture's real type.

tools.name: get_picture_upload_link
tools.description: Makes a link where the person adds their own photos to a website from their phone or computer, so the photos never pass through the conversation. Give them uploadUrl: it takes up to 10 photos of up to 20 MB each and works for 24 hours. Each photo is saved as images/, made smaller to suit a web page. When the person says they are done, list_website_files shows the saved paths to use as the src of an in the pages. Making the link changes nothing on the website. For photos already passed to you as files, save_website_pictures saves them directly.

websiteId.description: The websiteId start_website returned, or one list_sites shows.

editKey.description: The editKey start_website returned, which proves the website is the caller's. Leave it out for a website in the connected account.

tools.name: list_website_files
tools.description: Lists every file saved on a website, with each path and its size in bytes, beside the viewUrl, keepUrl, pages, passed and any problems. It changes nothing. The paths are the ones read_website_file and delete_website_file take; read_website_file on a photo shows it to you with its width and height. It also returns siteZip, an address that gives the whole website as one zip (curl -o site.zip) and takes one back (curl -T site.zip), for an AI that can run commands.

websiteId.description: The websiteId start_website returned, or one list_sites shows.

editKey.description: The editKey start_website returned, which proves the website is the caller's. Leave it out for a website in the connected account.

tools.name: read_website_file
tools.description: Returns one saved file from a website with its path, encoding and content: pages, stylesheets and scripts as utf8 text, and fonts as base64. A picture (such as a photo the person added) comes back as encoding picture with its contentType, bytes, width and height and no content; a smaller copy is attached as an image for you to look at, so you can see what it shows. It changes nothing. A path that is not saved fails with no_such_file; list_website_files shows which paths exist.

websiteId.description: The websiteId start_website returned, or one list_sites shows.

editKey.description: The editKey start_website returned, which proves the website is the caller's. Leave it out for a website in the connected account.

path.description: The file's path from the website's root, exactly as it was saved, such as index.html, about.html or images/shop.jpg. list_website_files shows every path.

tools.name: check_website_on_phone
tools.description: Opens a website's pages in a real browser at a phone's size (390 by 844, as an iPhone) and says, page by page, what a phone visitor would hit: sideways scrolling and what is too wide, pictures that do not load, text under 12px, links and buttons under 24px to tap, a missing or zoom-blocking viewport line, bars that cover the screen, and a main heading pushed below the first screen. Each page gets fine and findings in plain words. It changes nothing. Checks every page up to 5 (or the pages named), a few seconds each, up to 40 pages a day per website. With picture true it also returns a screenshot of the first page checked, for an app that can look at images. Fix what it finds with edit_website_file or save_website_files, then check those pages again. Fails with check_limit when the day's checks are used.

websiteId.description: The websiteId start_website returned, or one list_sites shows.

editKey.description: The editKey start_website returned, which proves the website is the caller's. Leave it out for a website in the connected account.

items.description: A saved page such as index.html or about.html.

pages.description: Optional: up to 5 saved pages to check, such as ["index.html", "menu.html"]. Leave it out to check every page, home page first, up to 5.

picture.description: true to also get a screenshot of the first page checked, as a phone shows it. Leave it out if your app cannot look at images.

tools.name: search_domains
tools.description: Asks a domain registrar, live, which names can be registered, and returns up to about a dozen, each with its name, whether it is available and whether it is premium. Availability can change at any moment. Nothing is bought or held; a name is bought from the website's keep page.

query.description: A whole domain name such as sweetcrumbs.com, or a word to build names from such as sweetcrumbs.

tools.name: delete_website
tools.description: Permanently deletes a whole website: every file, its address and its keep link. It cannot be undone. Call it only when the person has asked, in their own words, for the website to be deleted; never to start over, since save_website_files and edit_website_file change a website in place. To remove one file instead, use delete_website_file. A website with a plan is refused with has_a_plan; the person removes it from their dashboard.

websiteId.description: The websiteId start_website returned, or one list_sites shows.

editKey.description: The editKey start_website returned, which proves the website is the caller's. Leave it out for a website in the connected account.

tools.name: delete_website_file
tools.description: Removes one saved file from a website, then checks the remaining pages against the rules start_website returned, and returns the same report as save_website_files. Other files stay. A path that is not saved fails with no_such_file. Removing index.html leaves the website with no home page until one is saved. To delete the whole website, use delete_website.

websiteId.description: The websiteId start_website returned, or one list_sites shows.

editKey.description: The editKey start_website returned, which proves the website is the caller's. Leave it out for a website in the connected account.

path.description: The file's path from the website's root, exactly as it was saved, such as index.html, about.html or images/shop.jpg. list_website_files shows every path.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: Lists the websites in the person's Jaybird Digital account, sorted by name, with each one's id, name and live address. Websites started with start_website while the account was connected, or opened with their editKey, are listed under startedWebsites (up to 20, kept ones first). An account with none gets an empty list. Needs the person to connect their account; called without one, it asks them to sign in.
